label: Weidenbaum
info:
Energy/heating refactor v5.
Victron system/0/Ac/ActiveIn/Source: 0=not available, 1=grid, 2=generator, 3=shore, 240=inverting/island. This is the active source, not physical cable presence.
Victron systemcalc /Dc/Battery/Power: positive=charging, negative=discharging; >+30 W charging, <-30 W discharging, otherwise idle.
Existing PV/grid/SOC inputs are reused. Only two extra Victron reads are polled: battery power every 5s and active AC source every 10s.
v5 separates raw thermal demand from heating permission; logs control decisions and command/relay feedback separately; distinguishes motion receive timestamps from source timestamps.
DEBUG v5 records both source-event and Node-RED receive times; the pump controller's hourly age snapshot has its own evaluation timestamp.
Button event timestamps are normalized to Unix seconds; non-event messages no longer erase previous presses. StoreHeating/StoreClimate retain relay feedback as actual state and write command/stop reasons separately.
Heating/cooling active-use flags are aligned to actual relay feedback, not just an issued command; command age is used when attributing start/stop reasons.
Energy-state fan-out runs the heating controller first, so it updates effective demand before the cooling interlock evaluates that demand.

BLOCK 1 — temperature resolver emits normalized state, never raw sensor/timer messages
info: Sensirion prefers fresh aggregate data; Netatmo is fallback. The resolver uses sensirion_last_update and Netatmo sample timestamps, not keys that are never populated.

name: BLOCK 2 — energy state reuses PV/grid/SOC; adds battery power and AC source only
info: Existing Store Solar Power, Store Grid Power and Store Battery SoC remain the source of these values. Only two additional Victron signals are polled: system/0/Dc/Battery/Power (to detect discharge) and system/0/Ac/ActiveIn/Source (to know whether an AC source is connected even at 0 W grid power). No duplicate solar/grid/SOC subscription is added.

name: BLOCK 3 — heating and cooling consume derived state; heating demand releases cooling first
info: Heating has an absolute external-AC/grid interlock. Ordinary idle/comfort heat requires SoC > 80%; frost protection bypasses PV and SoC but not the grid interlock. Cooling starts only with fresh off-grid source data, SoC >=70%, PV >=1000 W, and no battery discharge; stops on low SOC or PV <400 W while running, with minimum compressor on/off guards.
